In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination therapy with hR1 and mTOR inhibitors is more effective than either agent alone in inhibiting RCC in vitro, and may provide a novel therapeutic approach in the treatment of advanced RCC.
the IGF-1 receptor is a valid therapeutic target in RCC and that the combination of an IGF-1-receptor inhibitor with an mTOR-inhibitor is an effective approach to treat this type of cancer.
the combination of IGF-1 receptor-targeting agents with mTOR inhibitors should be further evaluated in clinical trials for the treatment of RCC patients.

the combination of hR1-based IGF-1-R targeting agents with mTOR inhibitors may be a promising therapeutic option in RCC.

the DNL™ technology can be used to improve the efficacy of IGF-1 receptor-targeting agents, and that the combination of IGF- and mTOR-targeting agents could provide an alternative therapeutic strategy for the treatment of advanced or metastatic RCC.
the combination of IGF-1 receptor and mTOR inhibitors may be an effective therapeutic strategy for RCC.

combining IGF-IR-targeting agents with mTOR inhibitors may be a promising approach for the treatment of RCC.
the combination of IGF-1Rs targeting with mTOR inhibitors could be a new approach to treat RCC.
